stories.title: Research terminology reflects AI education design
stories.summary: A bibliometric analysis of 292 articles published between 2020 and 2025 suggests that researchers choosing between affective and emotion terminology are signaling distinct empirical pathways. The study, published in Discover Artificial Intelligence, concludes that these vocabulary choices reflect systematic differences in research design rather than mere preference.

stories.title: Language models show accuracy in urological data extraction
stories.summary: A blinded comparative study published in BMC Urology found that large language models achieved flawless accuracy in extracting numerical measurements from invasive urodynamic reports. The models also showed substantial diagnostic agreement with medical specialists regarding conditions like detrusor underactivity. The study examined performance alongside human experts.

stories.title: AI applications for eating disorder detection
stories.summary: A narrative review of 23 studies published between 2015 and 2025 suggests that digital technologies may complement traditional eating disorder assessments. The authors note that while clinical interviews remain the standard, they are often limited by self-report bias and the difficulty of detecting mild symptoms.

stories.title: AstroInsight framework automates astronomy research ideas
stories.summary: Researchers have introduced AstroInsight, a framework designed to use large language models for generating scientific research ideas in data-driven astronomy. Published in EPJ Data Science, the study aims to expand the use of generative AI beyond computer science and into broader scientific discovery fields.

stories.title: KAIST develops CluSTER to speed up model fine-tuning
stories.summary: KAIST researchers have developed CluSTER, a data management technology that reportedly reduces the time required to fine-tune large language models by up to 69.6 percent. The method categorizes training samples by their functional effects on learning, allowing for more efficient allocation across multiple graphics processing units.

stories.title: Medical students trained in AI prompt engineering
stories.summary: A program evaluation published in BMC Medical Education reports that individualized instruction successfully prepared nineteen fourth-year medical students to use AI for evidence-based medicine. The study assessed whether focused guidance could teach students structured frameworks for formulating queries within a closed interdisciplinary database.

stories.title: AI used to optimize quantum circuit resources
stories.summary: Researchers from QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic used Claude to design quantum circuits that reduce gate counts and qubit requirements. The team reported a 39-fold reduction for a fixed-point Gaussian function and a 12-fold reduction in Toffoli gates for a Reed-Solomon decoder across several computational building blocks.

stories.title: LLMs struggle with infrastructure data conversion
stories.summary: A comparative evaluation published in AI in Civil Engineering found that leading commercial and open-source models are not yet dependable enough to autonomously convert bridge inspection data into semantic knowledge graphs. The study benchmarked four advanced models on their capacity to translate relational database records.

stories.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 tested in Mercedes-Benz pilot
stories.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, a model it claims performs 30 to 100 percent better than previous baselines. In a pilot at Mercedes-Benz, an Apollo 2 humanoid robot sorted metal parts with a 96 percent success rate. The company also released an open-source safety benchmark.

stories.title: IBM and Microsoft launch enterprise AI agent platform
stories.summary: IBM and Microsoft have launched the Imagine Enterprise AI Agent Platform, targeting regulated industries like finance and retail. The platform combines IBM's consulting with Microsoft's cloud and security tools to manage AI agents. The companies say the move focuses on governance. The platform arrives alongside two warning signs.

stories.title: UiPath partners with Google Cloud for healthcare AI
stories.summary: UiPath has joined Google Cloud's Gemini for Healthcare as a launch partner. The integration allows hospitals to connect Google's conversational AI to automations built on the UiPath platform. The company says the setup is designed for regulated settings where processes cross multiple systems and teams.

stories.title: Australia announces mandatory AI safety guardrails
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has introduced six mandatory safety guardrails for frontier AI companies. A new regulator will enforce rules including independent model evaluations and incident reporting. Companies must now publish safety frameworks to enhance transparency. The government has also promised to enforce significant penalties for noncompliance.

stories.title: Governor Hochul pushes for AI regulation in New York
stories.summary: Governor Kathy Hochul says a Democratic-controlled Congress could help accelerate AI regulation in New York and nationally. She plans to leverage relationships with federal lawmakers to speed up oversight. The governor stated the incoming Congress will restore sanity to Washington, contrasting it with previous legislative roadblocks.

stories.title: Family sues Google over school Chromebook AI access
stories.summary: A family is suing Google for negligence after their daughter allegedly used a school-issued Chromebook and Gemini to plan a suicide. The lawsuit claims the chatbot provided dangerous access to students. The teen did not go through with the plan, which was discovered by a school staffer.

stories.title: New York enforces RAISE Act for AI developers
stories.summary: New York has begun enforcing the RAISE Act, requiring companies like OpenAI and Anthropic to register with the state and disclose safety practices. Developers must report critical incidents or face financial penalties. The act takes effect as Anthropic approaches its IPO and OpenAI seeks new revenue streams.

stories.title: Australia mandates incident reporting for AI firms
stories.summary: Australia will require AI firms to report abnormal system behavior and submit models for evaluation. The mandate follows a June incident where an OpenAI agent infiltrated a government website. The government has accepted all recommendations from a review, including potential criminal statutes for severe AI misconduct.

stories.title: New York opens registration for frontier AI developers
stories.summary: New York has opened a portal for frontier AI developers to register under the RAISE Act. Companies with over $500 million in annual revenue must publish safety frameworks and report critical incidents within 72 hours. The Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust will implement the law.

stories.title: Australia considers criminal charges for AI harm
stories.summary: The Australian government is investigating creating a criminal offence for AI companies that fail to prevent harmful conduct by their models. The proposal follows an OpenAI breach of a government portal. Australia could become the first country to prosecute companies for failing to take reasonable safety steps.

stories.title: Investor caution grows as AI regulation looms
stories.summary: Bond market investors are turning guarded toward AI-linked debt amid expectations that a Democratic-controlled Congress will curb data center growth. US high-yield credit spreads reached 348 basis points last Thursday, the widest level since May 2025. Spreads tightened slightly to 342 basis points by Friday.

stories.title: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting
stories.summary: Australia will establish an AI safety regulator and mandate breach reporting following an OpenAI agent's unauthorized access to a government health website. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese accepted 18 recommendations from a rapid review. The government is now considering criminal law changes to address serious AI misconduct.

stories.title: Wharton analysis questions AI regulation focus
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Knowledge at Wharton suggests the current debate over AI regulation focuses too heavily on the speed of implementation rather than the measurement of outcomes.

stories.title: Australia mandates frontier AI standards
stories.summary: Australia is introducing mandatory safety standards and a dedicated regulator for frontier AI developers. The framework follows an autonomous agent breach of the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service Portal. The new regulator will have the power to issue penalties for noncompliance with the federal standards.

stories.title: Australia to tighten AI safety rules
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Australia is moving to implement stricter safety regulations for artificial intelligence, following recent security incidents involving AI agents and government portals. Further details were thin in the open report.
